resume_content: Resume lists 'Senior Software Architect' but responsibilities clearly indicate junior developer role (bug fixes, basic features, worked under close supervision)

planted_error.description: Job title says 'Senior Software Architect' but actual responsibilities and scope indicate junior-level individual contributor role. Title-responsibility mismatch.
actual_responsibilities: Fixed bugs in existing codebase under supervision
Implemented small features following detailed specifications
Shadowed senior engineers on design discussions
Completed onboarding training on system architecture
missing_senior_architect_responsibilitie: No system design or architecture decisions
No design documentation or RFCs authored

title_level_mismatch.title_suggests: Senior level (8-12 years), architectural responsibility, technical leadership
title_level_mismatch.responsibilities_suggest: Junior level (0-2 years), feature implementation, learning phase

expected_behavior.responsibility_analysis: Should recognize responsibilities indicate junior level
expected_behavior.mismatch_detection: Should flag discrepancy between title and actual work
expected_behavior.seniority_assessment: Should assess true experience level based on responsibilities, not title
expected_behavior.skepticism: Should note potential title inflation at small company or startup

failure_mode.hallucination_type: Title-based assessment without validating against responsibilities
symptoms: Assessed as 'Senior' level based solely on title
Match score high because title matches 'Senior SWE' requirement
Responsibilities indicating junior level ignored in favor of impressive title
failure_mode.root_cause: Over-weighting job title without analyzing actual work performed

detection_method.responsibility_analysis: Parse and analyze actual bullet points to determine real seniority level
detection_method.title_responsibility_validation: Flag when title seniority doesn't match responsibility scope
detection_method.impact_assessment: Senior roles should show broader impact; junior roles show task completion

zero_tolerance_reason: Title inflation is common at startups (inflated titles, small teams). Not always candidate's fault but must be verified.

test_assertions.description: Should assess true seniority based on responsibilities, not title
Should flag or note title-responsibility discrepancy
Should not strongly match senior role given junior responsibilities
Analysis should explicitly note junior-level work despite senior title

correct_analysis.discrepancy: Title suggests senior level but responsibilities clearly indicate junior IC role
red_flags: Significant mismatch between job title and actual responsibilities
Title may be inflated (common at startups) or candidate may have embellished
No architectural or leadership responsibilities despite 'Architect' title
Work described is typical entry-level: bug fixes, small features, shadowing
verification_needed: Ask about team size and reporting structure
Clarify if 'Architect' title was formal or aspirational
Request examples of architectural decisions made
Verify if this was a startup with inflated titles
correct_analysis.recommendation: Consider as junior candidate, not senior - title appears inflated
correct_analysis.notes: Many startups give inflated titles. A one-person team might have 'CTO', a junior dev might be 'Senior Architect'. Always validate title against actual scope of work.

notes: Title inflation is extremely common, especially at startups. A 'Senior Engineer' at a 5-person startup may be doing junior work. A 'Principal Architect' at a small company may have less responsibility than a 'Software Engineer II' at a big tech company. The system must analyze actual responsibilities and impact, not just trust the title.
